The term was proposed by Berzelius.
On the basis of arrangement of the atoms within molecules there are two broad classes of isomerism. They are i) structural isomerism and ii) stereoisomerism.

Two or more organic compounds which have the same molecular formula but different arrangement of the parent chain of carbon atoms are called chain isomers and the phenomenon is called chain isomerism.

Two or more compounds having same molecular formula, but have different functional groups are called functional isomers. The property shown by these compounds is called functional isomerism. Functional isomers have different physical as well as chemical properties due to the presence of different functional groups. The following pairs of compounds represent functional isomers. a. Alcohols and ethers (CnH2n+2O) b. Aldehydes and ketones (CnH2nO) c. Carboxylic acid and esters (CnH2nO2)
